ca_nature_trail_wall.blurb: A low, slabby wall at the Indian Cove end of Joshua Tree, tucked above the desert floor beside the paved campground loop road. It holds 11 short climbs, mostly gear-protected with a single bolted line and one top-rope, and the grades stay friendly: a few at the easiest end, a cluster of 5.6 to 5.8 lines, and just one harder 5.10. The rock is monzogranite, and the smearing style rewards careful footwork. With a walk of only a few minutes and a north to northwest lean, it suits beginners and anyone wanting a quick, mellow session.

ca_iceberg_2.blurb: A single large boulder in the Icebergs group, high in the San Jacinto Mountains at roughly 8,500 feet, in the Tramway bouldering zone. It sits a few steps uphill from the neighbouring Iceberg 1 boulder. The 11 problems cover a wide range, from V0 up to a V10, with a handful of easy and moderate lines, a couple in the V4 to V6 range, and two standout hard problems on the big face. The hillside is steep, and the long uphill walk in keeps crowds thin compared with other Tramway areas. Bring a crash pad and expect a committing day.

ca_outpost_the_2.blurb: A small sport crag among the Tatooine group on Fairview Mountain, in the high desert of Apple Valley at about 3,900 feet. Ten of its 11 routes are bolted, with one crack climb, and almost everything falls between 5.10 and 5.11, with a lone 5.9 as the way in. The rock quality is good and the belay ledge is shaded, which helps on warm days. It is a modest wall rather than a big destination, best combined with its neighbours on the same hillside by climbers who are comfortable on 5.10 and up.

ca_fisherman_s_buttress_west_face.blurb: The broad west side of Fisherman's Buttress on the south shore of Big Bear Lake, in the San Bernardino Mountains at close to 7,000 feet among the Highway 18 crags. Its 11 routes mix bolted lines, a few top-ropes and two gear climbs, running from an easy 5.5 up to 5.12, with most of the weight in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The face is cleaner than the neighbouring east side, with far less lichen, though the rock texture is rough and grippy. A trail through pines leads to the base; the path beneath the face runs just above the road and is loose, so keep rocks off the pavement.

ca_failsafe_wall.blurb: A short west-facing wall rising straight from the water in the Upper Gorge of Owens River Gorge, near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra. The river splits it into two sectors, directly opposite Warm Out Wall. Most of the 11 routes are bolted, with two gear lines, and the grades start near 5.9 then climb through the 5.10s and 5.11s into the low 5.12s, so it suits strong intermediates and up. The wall is roughly 40 feet tall and picks up late-afternoon shade, and evaporation off the river keeps belayers cool on warm days. It sees few climbers.

ca_gateway_rock_2.blurb: A chunky formation beside the Real Hidden Valley trailhead in Joshua Tree, at about 4,200 feet, only a short stroll from the car. Its 11 climbs are all crack and face lines on gear, plus one top-rope option, and the grades run from an easy 5.7 to 5.11, with the bulk sitting at 5.10. The rock is rough and grippy, split by clean cracks, making it a good place to practise jamming and gear placement. Some of the routes sit on the north face, though the rock still soaks up desert sun, so an early start helps in summer.
